title: Advertising Guidelines for Tuition and Private Education Services to Prevent Fear-based Marketing
what_it_is: Advertising Guidelines for Tuition and Private Education Services to Prevent Fear-based Marketing

sections.label: MOE reviewing tuition advertising measures
sections.summary: MOE is reviewing measures to discourage undesirable advertising by tuition and private education providers, while all Singapore advertisements are subject to the Singapore Code of Advertising Practice.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) is reviewing the measures needed to discourage undesirable advertising practices by tuition and private education providers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Currently, all advertisements in Singapore, including for tuition services, are already subject to the Singapore Code of Advertising Practice.

sections.label: Advertising Code on inducing demand
sections.summary: Under the Code of Advertising Practice, advertisements should not capitalise on anxieties to induce demand for tuition services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: In line with the Code of Advertising Practice, the advertisements should not capitalise on anxieties to induce demand for tuition services.

sections.label: MOE engaging on education arms race
sections.summary: In the coming months, MOE will engage parents, students and educators on reducing the education arms race and attendant anxieties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: In the coming months, MOE will be engaging parents, students and educators to see how we can continue to reduce the "arms race" in education and attendant anxieties.

sections.label: MOE studying options, reporting egregious claims
sections.summary: MOE is reviewing measures, will study options without rushing, says providers have been generally responsible, and the public can report egregious claims to the Advertising Standards Authority of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier, MOE is reviewing the measures needed to discourage any undesirable advertising practices by the tuition industry.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: We will carefully study our options, but we also do not want to rush into implementing any additional measures.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: Thus far, as far as we can tell, tuition and other private education providers have generally been responsible in their advertisements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
sentences.text: To the Member's second question, in relation to fearmongering in the online context especially, our position is such that if parents or members of the public find that there are some egregious or outlandish claims with regard to tuition, they can also file a report with the Advertising Standards Authority of Singapore, which is an advisory council under the Consumers Association of Singapore.
